title: Roll R Way settles with U.S. Attorney's Office over ADA access for disabled patrons
text:
Roll R Way settles with U.S. Attorney’s Office over ADA access for disabled patrons
The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced on July 8 a civil settlement with Roll R Way, a skating center operating in York, Chambersburg, and Donora, to ensure compliance with Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act.
U.S. Attorney Brian D. Miller said that his office received several complaints from families whose children with Type 1 Diabetes were refused entry at Roll R Way when they attempted to bring necessary diabetes treatment supplies, including small amounts of food and drink required to regulate blood sugar. The skating center's management denied these families entry due to its 'no outside food or drink' policy. According to Miller, this failure to accommodate prevented access for these families and created a barrier for others who may have diabetes, food allergies, or other dietary restrictions.
Under the terms of the settlement agreement, Roll R Way is required to revise its policy on outside food and drink so that reasonable accommodations are made for patrons with diabetes and other dietary needs. The company will also train employees on the new accommodation policy and provide public notice about how customers can request an accommodation if needed. Additionally, Roll R Way will pay $500 to each complainant family.
Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act prohibits public accommodations such as family amusement centers from excluding people with disabilities from enjoying goods, services, privileges, facilities, and advantages provided by those businesses. Information about federal disability rights statutes is available through ADA.gov or by calling the Department of Justice’s toll-free ADA information line.
The settlement was reached without an admission of liability by Roll R Way in order to avoid litigation costs and burdens. Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael J. Butler represented the government during both investigation and settlement proceedings.
The U.S. Attorney for the Middle District of Pennsylvania serves approximately 3.2 million residents across 21,907 square miles in central Pennsylvania; it operates under the United States Department of Justice from facilities in Harrisburg, Scranton, Williamsport and Wilkes-Barre; it handles federal prosecutions as well as civil litigation on behalf of the government while promoting community safety initiatives such as Project Safe Neighborhoods, according to the official website.
